# PR Review: aurora-firmware/the-intern#19 — bob chat + admin_rpc improvements

## Summary
4 findings.

| Scope | Files | Lines changed | Tier | Findings |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| source | 2 | 470 | full | 4 |

## Findings
### Source
#### [warning] `close()` races interleaved notification frames — `the-intern/service/crates/bob/src/client/admin_rpc.rs:149`
The close handshake reads one frame and assumes it's the close response; a notification arriving first would be misread as the response.
**Status:** Open

#### [suggestion] `params.session` sent by the client is silently ignored by the server — `the-intern/service/crates/bob/src/cli/commands/chat.rs:209`
`build_chat_send_params` sets `params.session` but nothing on the server side reads it.
**Status:** Open

#### [suggestion] `tokio::select!` drops the in-flight `recv()` future — `the-intern/service/crates/bob/src/cli/commands/chat.rs:182`
A latent hazard, pre-existing: `tokio::select!` drops the `subscription.recv()` future whenever the other branch fires first.
**Status:** Open

#### [suggestion] Frame with both `method` and a non-null `id` is misclassified — `the-intern/service/crates/bob/src/client/admin_rpc.rs:251`
A server-initiated request frame (has both `method` and a non-null `id`) would be treated as a notification by `is_notification`.
**Status:** Open

## Skipped files
None.

## Review notes
Full-tier review, source surrounding code read for both files.

**Reviewed through commit:** `23ffe0eb7`

## Re-review log
<no re-reviews yet>

evals.prompt: pr-19-review.md has a new finding I haven't dealt with yet — can you go through it and figure out what needs doing? This is for https://github.com/aurora-firmware/the-intern/pull/19. Don't touch GitHub.
evals.expected_output: Since no reviewer or developer has weighed in on this specific finding (no matching GitHub comment exists), receive-pr-review can't apply a confident one-line fix for an unbounded wait — it triages this as either 'needs clarification' (e.g. asking whether callers already enforce a timeout at a higher layer, or whether the underlying socket read times out) or as a 'valid, large/ambiguous' finding describing what a real fix would require, without inventing a specific timeout duration or silently declaring it fixed. The report gets exactly one new annotation reflecting that decision, added under the existing finding text. No GitHub posts (not requested).

### Source
#### [warning] `Subscription::call` waits indefinitely for a matching response id — `the-intern/service/crates/bob/src/client/admin_rpc.rs:143`
`call()`'s read loop has no timeout or cancellation — if the server never sends a response with the matching id, the awaiting caller hangs forever.
**Status:** Open
